[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60769098]While Drømm admired the architecture silently, his head turning on a swivel at the beauty of the moment, Malben, ever the politician and revolutionary would speak,

Firstly, we thank you for your memorandae, they have provided a clean blueprint by which we can adapt to the Citharo line, now if you shall permit my long tonguedness (A saying for which means he was about to go into a speech of dialectalism) I shall now enlighten you of the matter of Thýven.

The matter that currently stands is that Thýven is a nation of disunity at the present, torn between the old order, the moderates, and the revolution. It is a symptom of the fact that true unity has never been established in Thýven, which long held to either autocracy or devolution, thereby creating a strange fusion of autonomy and nationalism.

It is thus that I find, as noted in my memo, that the centralisation of the revolution is impossible without causing further discord. Of course it isnt a question of willingness but one of order, for the old order believes itself semi-secure under federalism, though they are wising up to the present moment that the people are turning, but if they for a moment believe themselves to be in danger, my position is at danger, for they can seize upon the disorder and make unto themselves the victors,[/quote]
"The revolution is never an easy thing." Lo Pilato lamented, seating everyone at the table. "People think that they are the revolution by having waved a flag or torched a rich man's car. That is anarchy. Other says the revolution comes from the implementation of reform and the improvement of the quality of life, which is gradualism. Others still that the revolution is the elimination of the old by guillotine, murder. Others still that the revolution is somehow such a sweeping and powerful torrent that cleanses all things, that a revolution simply 'breaks out' and is."

"It isn't?" Terrasi queried, tilting her head. "Revolutions happen when we least expect it, no? I definitely didn't expect to wake up one day and see red flags flying in Sanguivallis y'know. I'm pretty sure the Gythenans definitely didn't plan things out either."

"All revolutions start with misery, comrade Terrasi." Lo Pilato replied, leaning back in his chair to draw two parallel lines in the air. It was the two systems. "Every revolution starts because of the dialectic. Capitalism destroys, therefore the people revolt for socialism. But misery does not give rise to mindless revolutions. At every moment before the spark is the vanguard that mobilizes the proletariat. Fascists seem to think that we just stumble into revolution, or that in our misery we had taken shortcuts after failing to acknowledge wiser options. And yet, I am free, while they are chained."

Lo Pilato then turned to Malben, at last revisiting his concerns.

"Comrade Malben, the revolution is always a minority position. Do you know why there is a vanguard party? Because there are many proletarians, but only so many revolutionaries. In this world filled with greed, the proletariat slave away through cycles of torment and dismemberment, bludgeoned by a master incapable of ever understanding their pain, and they continue to do so, believing that at the end of this great struggle, they at least still keep their hide. Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth! It is for this reason that we create the vanguard party in the minority position, because we understand what must be done to free the proletariat from bondage. The old ways and the old policy can never understand the vanguard, which is why they bitterly oppose us, but they will eventually understand. At the very least, I commend you for having made it this far. The liberation of all nations is happening everywhere, the final victory now is for the minority to enrapture the proletariat and become the majority. And if the imperialists try and opposing you, the Sanguinians will always have more than enough resources to help."
